title: A Woodpecker Slams Its Head Into Wood 12,000 Times a Day

scenes.text: A woodpecker slams its head into wood 12,000 times a day.
Each hit is about a thousand G. Enough to concuss a human instantly.
It hammers around 20 times a second, its beak moving at 7 metres per second.
For years, scientists thought its skull was a shock absorber. In 2022, they filmed it at high speed. It isn't.
The head stops dead, like a hammer. The brain survives only because it's tiny. 700 times smaller than yours.
Twelve thousand hits a day. Zero headaches.

description:
A woodpecker hits its head against wood about 12,000 times a day, with each strike decelerating at roughly 1,000 G.
Biologists long assumed the skull cushioned the brain. A 2022 study in Current Biology filmed woodpeckers at high speed and found the head stops rigidly, like a hammer; the brain survives because it is tiny, about 700 times smaller than a human brain, so the same deceleration does far less damage.
Would you survive one day as a woodpecker? Comment below.
first_comment: Engineers once copied the woodpecker skull to design helmets and black boxes. Turns out the real trick is just a very small brain. What other animal would you want to borrow a body part from?
